svg.title: The Lands of the Book of Mormon: an imagined map (v2)
svg.desc: An imagined map drawn only from directions, distances and elevation cues stated in the Book of Mormon text. Scholars' readings are marked as inferences. It does not show, and makes no claim about, any real-world place. The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints takes no position on the real-world location of Book of Mormon events.

g.text: sea north and sea south are named once, Helaman 3:8; some writers read them as figurative
"an isle of the sea" (2 Nephi 10:20). The land is drawn nearly surrounded by water (Alma 22:32).
called the land of Mulek (Helaman 6:10); "covered with large bodies of water" (Alma 50:29; Helaman 3:4)
the land southward, called the land of Lehi (Helaman 6:10)
a narrow strip of wilderness, east sea to west sea (Alma 22:27; 50:8)

svg.text: lower Sidon: the text never names its outlet;
the east sea is Clark's and Sorenson's inference
position inferred: Sorenson east of centre, Clark near centre
line Bountiful and Desolation: a day and a half's journey,
fortified line, a day's journey, west sea to the east

g.text: Aaron uncertain: Alma 8:13 and 50:14 pull it apart
lists it captured, a probable scribal slip
Moroni sank into the sea (3 Nephi 8:9)
up to Nephi, down to Zarahemla (Omni 1:13; Mosiah 7:2-6)
"over" to Melek (Alma 8:3); higher ground is Clark's inference
Hagoth's ship into the west sea,
Mormon's retreat, Zarahemla to Cumorah (Mormon 1 to 6), dotted
order as listed; positions of the towns on it are inferred
Omer's flight: Moron, past Shim and
Shiz and Coriantumr: three days' fight
the losers fled "southward" from Ripliancum to Ogath (Ether 15:8-10)
named, with a stated relation to another place
named; position is an inference, not stated
extent, outlet or placement not stated in the text
"up" or "down" in the text; arrow points uphill
a journey with the day count the text gives
a longer route, stops in the order the text lists them
Shapes, sizes and sea outlines are invented. Only the relations
and day counts come from the text. Inferences are labelled.
places the text names without a position the map can show
stops on Mormon's retreat before Joshua (Mormon 2:4-5)
valleys and hill of the last Jaredite wars (Ether 14:27-28)
coast not stated (Ether 6:12); Sorenson leans west
south by the west sea; by the seashore (Alma 56:14, 31)
east of Sidon (Alma 2:15); borders of Manti (Alma 43:31)
lost many days in a land of many waters; found
last Jaredite, found by the people of Zarahemla (Omni 1:21)
plains between Mulek and Bountiful (Alma 52:20); Gid
inland of Mulek is Sorenson's reading (Helaman 5:14-15)
Narrow neck, small neck, narrow pass
Spacing follows Clark's rule of thumb for proportions only:
Nephi to Zarahemla about nine days, the neck about four
days wide, Cumorah about six days north of Bountiful.
Those are his estimates, not the text.
Sorenson's chapter gives thirteen days for the valley of
Alma to Zarahemla; the text says twelve (Mosiah 24:25).
Some writers argue Sidon flows south. This map follows
the text's "up" to Manti and "down" to Zarahemla.
THE LANDS OF THE BOOK OF MORMON
An imagined map, drawn only from directions, distances and elevation cues in the text
Illustrative only. Shapes, sizes and distances are invented to fit the text's own clues. Scholars' readings are marked as inferences.
It does not show, and makes no claim about, any real-world location.
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints takes no position on the real-world location of Book of Mormon events (Gospel Topics, Book of Mormon Geography).
Verses, all checked against churchofjesuschrist.org on 2026-10-26: Omni 1:13, 21; 2 Nephi 5:8; 10:20; Mosiah 7:1-6; 8:8; 9:4, 8; 11:12-13; 18:4-5; 21:25-26; 23:3-4; 24:20, 25;
Readings marked as inferences follow John E. Clark, "A Key for Evaluating Nephite Geographies" (1989) and John L. Sorenson, Mormon's Map (2000). See changes-v2.md for sources.
